shared_elements: frontal, bilaterally symmetrical relief composition on the main face
stacked/tiered motifs along a central vertical axis
broad upper zone reading as headdress or crown
tapering block set on a base
justification: Both show a tall, tapering stone shaft carved in low relief with a strictly symmetrical, axially stacked sequence of face-like motifs and roundels beneath a broad crowning headdress zone, so the underlying compositional scheme is comparable. The biggest difference is density and handling: B is a dense, deeply undercut, intricate carving reproduced as a fine-line engraving, while A is a heavily eroded, simplified, sparse relief on a rounded boulder-like form recorded photographically.
